chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: Jam sessions at Minton's and the coming of bebop; Thelonious Monk
summary: It was where Caldwell met Dizzy, Parker and Monk; he remembers Monk as a normal pianist who changed his style.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Well now, I mean did you just -- did your group just play there, or did that become a place like it did in later years, where people came to sit in?
That's where it first started. That's where I met Dizzy, Charlie Parker, Thelonius Monk. We'd get off the bands and I'd say, go up there and play something, buy them drinks.
So that -- how soon did that begin? You opened there in '41. I mean this bebop thing begins what, a year or two later?
That came a year or two years later

because that was between Charlie and Dizzy, (unintelligible). They made the bebop popular, and they were about the only ones could play it decently anyway, what I think, because I understood it very well (unintelligible) because Charlie and I did a little, you know, off hand social session together and different, you know, different groups. We'd go to Jersey and advertise us. Him and I were very good buddies, very close friends; Charlie and I were very close friends, Dizzy too. But he was a good man.
Well, what -- now, some people have said, have told me that in those days, you know, before he'd gotten into these sort of bebop things, Thelonius used to play more like a normal piano player.
Well, there are many -- in other words, he had more technique than you might think.
You know, that's a very unusual thing for a man--
-- to go in the direction that makes you think he has--
Right. But he always wanted to be

included in that particular set up, and he probably wanted to change his style to fit what they were doing. I think that's the only thing, what it actually amounted to, because when I heard him after he got, you know, big, I said this is not the guy that I've known, always used to come down there and sit in and play piano with us all the time. But he wasn't doing nothing, in my estimation.

A lot of people just go in there and at the Apollo giblet, Thelonius Monk (unintelligible), that son of a bitch can't play nothing. He didn't know I was a musician, (Unintelligible). But the guy didn't know I was a musician. I'm sitting there listening.
